directions: Wildwood Purity is a white-flowered selection of hardy begonia distinguished by leaf undersides that flush a deeper, more saturated blood-red than the species typically shows, giving strong two-tone color even before the flowers open. Clusters of pure white blooms appear from summer into fall above compact, bushy clumps. Grow in bright shade to full shade in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil, and mulch over winter in the colder part of its range since the plant dies to the ground and resprouts from tubers each spring. Like other hardy begonia selections it self-sows modestly via small axillary bulbils, so established clumps slowly widen into a patch over a few seasons.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

directions: Early Bird is a hardy begonia selection resulting from a cross between the species and the white-flowered Chinese form Begonia grandis subsp. sinensis 'Shanxi White', combining bright chartreuse to lime-green foliage with pale pink flower clusters. It begins blooming several weeks ahead of typical hardy begonia, extending the shade garden's late-season color into high summer. Grow in bright shade with consistently moist, humus-rich soil; plants die back hard at frost and return reliably from tubers the following spring. Its lighter leaf color gives it a distinct look next to the darker-leaved standard hardy begonia and other named selections.

directions: This Chinese subspecies selection was collected from a moist rock crevice in Shanxi Province and is grown for its compact habit and abundant pure white flower clusters that open from midsummer into fall over light green foliage. It forms a tidier, lower clump than typical hardy begonia, making it useful toward the front of a shaded border or rock garden. Give it humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in bright shade, and let the tubers overwinter undisturbed under a protective mulch layer in the colder part of its range. Like other Begonia grandis selections it spreads gradually by small bulbils that form along the stems and drop to the soil in autumn.
